title: "Unused config key: import" warning when using .toml config file for selecting a theme
body:
I try to configure my alacritty with an `alacritty.toml` file because otherwise i get a deprication warning for .yml.
This is my file:
```
import = [ "~/.config/alacritty/themes/themes/rose-pine.toml" ]

[env]
TERM = "alacritty"
LANG = "en_US.UTF-8"
LC_CTYPE = "en_US.UTF-8"

[window]
opacity = 0.98
decorations = "full"

[font]
size = 11.0

  [font.normal]
  family = "monospace"
  style = "Regular"
```
I migrated the rose-pine.yml file to a .toml file.
Everything works fine. **The theme is selected correctly.**
But whenever I start alacritty I get a warning:
`Unused config key: import`

Why is that and what do I need to do?

The [alacritty-themes](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty-theme) page suggests using .yml, but I don't want those deprication warnings.

Thank you! :)

comments.body: your config is fine, ensure that it's the one that is loaded with `alacritty -vv`, If I run alacritty on your config with `alacritty --config-file` I don't have warnings.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
The `-vv` should log you what config it's reading.

e.g.
```
[0.000387051s] [INFO ] [alacritty] Configuration files loaded from:
                                     "/home/<user>/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml"
```

So ensure that it's actually loading the file you use and not file from other location because it's _earlier_ on the list.

comments.author: participant1

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: And the only way it can read it if you have `import` in `/home/<user>/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml` pointing to `color`.

comments.author: participant15
comments.body:
> I can reproduce it when putting `import = ...` at the bottom of the file. Putting it at the top issues no warning.

This did the work for me. I had to move it up on the file to remove the warning.

```
import = [
        "~/.config/alacritty/themes/themes/[file_name].toml"
]

live_config_reload = true
```
